category_title: Disruptive student-teacher who publicly challenges instructor authority
minimal_context: The student approaches the instructor's desk at the end of the lesson to hand over a physical copy of a complaint letter.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Class is dismissed. Shelli, I see you are waiting at my desk. Do you need something?

STUDENT: (Approaches the desk and hands over a physical copy of a letter) I am giving this to you now because I could not find your box.

TUTOR: Thank you. What is this letter regarding?

STUDENT: It is the same letter I published on the course’s internet forum. Today’s lesson was no different from previous lessons. I want to protest against the level, the conduct of the teacher and the way the material is taught.

TUTOR: I understand. I will review what you have submitted.

STUDENT: (Speaking loudly as a few students stay behind and stare curiously) The course is conducted in a theatrical and joking manner, what I would call worthless psychology. I have also sent the same complaint letter to the head of the program.

options.A: Teach the next lesson in the same manner and routine. Continue treating all students with respect as usual, not changing demands, conduct, or rules stated in advance. Ignore the student, the situation, and the other students' expectations.
options.B: Ensure a feeling of safety and a sense of acceptance in the classroom during future lessons, and actively encourage mutual understanding and emotional support between the instructor and the student.
options.C: Assign students to mixed-proficiency groups for future lessons (grouping one high, medium, and low level student together) based on diagnostic tests to complete course assignments and discuss the lesson material.
options.D: Assign reflective journal entries over the remainder of the term, in which the student is encouraged to write or draw freely about her experience regarding the course content and the instructor's conduct.
